questions.prompt: Do you like to keep things tidy?

answers.basic: Yes, I like knowing where everything is. At work that goes for files and notes as much as the things on my desk. If a teammate asks about a decision from last week, I like being able to find the note while we're still talking.

questions.prompt: Did you keep your room tidy as a child?

answers.basic: My room was fairly messy as a child. I'd leave books or sports gear out and put them away when I was asked. My badminton gear was usually the first thing I dropped by the door because I knew I'd want it again the next day.

questions.prompt: How do you keep your work or study space tidy?

answers.basic: I keep just the things I'm using on my desk. On my computer I try to give files clear names so I can find them again. For example, I keep notes for each project together, so I can pick up where I left off without searching through downloads.

questions.prompt: Do you think that it is necessary to be tidy?

answers.basic: Some tidiness is useful because it saves time. I care more about being able to find things than about getting every object to line up. A desk can look a bit lived-in, and I'm happy as long as I can put my hands on the right notebook.
